articles.title: Sharat Saxena, 76, Shares Standing MRI Photos Ahead of Lumbar Spine Surgery
articles.excerpt: The veteran Bollywood actor, last seen in Son of Sardaar 2, posted pictures from Mumbai's Bombay Hospital and told fans he hopes to walk properly and work again.
articles.nri_angle: Saxena's films from Mr. India to Baghban remain staples in NRI households, making his health update one diaspora families follow closely.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A.R. Rahman Announces Mumbai and Delhi Dates for The Wonderment Tour
articles.excerpt: The Oscar-winning composer brings his stadium-scale Wonderment Tour to Mumbai's Jio World Garden on November 1 and Delhi's Backyard Sports Club on November 21, with tickets exclusively on District by Zomato.
articles.nri_angle: Rahman's global tour schedule includes US dates (Texas Oct 29, 2026; Carnegie Hall May 2027), and the India shows give NRI fans reason to plan trips home — the same catalogue fills stadiums in both countries.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: AR Rahman Was Told Not to Work With Danny Boyle — He Won Two Oscars Instead
articles.excerpt: Warned that Danny Boyle might throw out his score, Rahman composed the Slumdog Millionaire music in secret over three weeks — and collected two Oscars, two Grammys, a Golden Globe and a BAFTA.
articles.image_caption: AR Rahman holds a vintage microphone against a blue backdrop. Rahman has recalled that his agent warned him against scoring Slumdog Millionaire — he composed it in secret in three weeks and won two Oscars.
articles.nri_angle: An iconic Indian-artist-on-world-stage story — the diaspora takes pride in Rahman's Oscars and the 'Jai Ho' cultural moment, and the trust-your-instincts arc is strong human interest.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Rani Mukerji Accepts Raj Kapoor Award in Marathi, Marks Three Decades in Cinema
articles.excerpt: The actor received the Raj Kapoor Special Contribution Award at the 62nd Maharashtra State Film Awards, where she spoke in Marathi about Mumbai and Maharashtra shaping her identity and career.
articles.image_caption: Rani Mukerji, in a green saree, holds her award at the Maharashtra State Film Awards ceremony. She received the Raj Kapoor Special Contribution Award on September 9 and delivered her acceptance speech in Marathi.
articles.nri_angle: Rani Mukerji's three-decade career — from Black to Mrs Chatterjee vs Norway — has a large diaspora following; the Marathi-language acceptance speech is a cultural moment for the community.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Floating Cinema Brings Bollywood Classics to Srinagar's Dal Lake
articles.excerpt: Srinagar's Dal Lake became an open-air cinema as the inaugural Jammu & Kashmir film festival screened Bollywood classics to audiences on shikaras and the lakefront.
articles.image_caption: Houseboats on Dal Lake in Srinagar, Jammu and Kashmir. The floating cinema of the International Film Festival of Jammu & Kashmir screened Bollywood classics from the lakefront, with audiences watching in shikaras.
articles.nri_angle: For diaspora audiences who grew up on these classics, the floating cinema revives a shared cinematic inheritance — Kashmir's Bollywood-era imagery shown on the water where it was filmed.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: 'Hunkkaar' Trailer: Aneet Padda's Student Accuses Powerful Godman of Abuse
articles.excerpt: The JioHotstar series, streaming September 25, casts Aneet Padda as a 17-year-old who accuses a revered godman of abuse — with Fatima Sana Shaikh as the cop investigating the case.
articles.nri_angle: The JioHotstar series premieres simultaneously for viewers in India and abroad, with Priyanka Chopra Jonas as executive producer — a diaspora icon backing a socially anchored Hindi story for a global audience.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Hema Malini Credits 'Hanuman Ji Ki Kripa' for 'Hanuman Ansh' Rs 150-Crore Run
articles.excerpt: The veteran actor said she was "very happy" the Neem Karoli Baba devotional drama became a box-office phenomenon, and praised first-time producer Anupriya Nagar for backing it.
articles.image_caption: Image: @ZoomTV via X
articles.nri_angle: Hanuman Ansh releases internationally on September 11, 2026, bringing the sleeper devotional hit to diaspora theatres in the US, UK and Gulf.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Preity Zinta Recalls How Manisha Koirala Made Her Feel She 'Belonged' in Bollywood
articles.excerpt: Ahead of her comeback film Vibe, Zinta told The Indian Express that Koirala's warmth on the Dil Se set gave her the confidence to start her film journey.
articles.image_caption: Preity Zinta in a still from the teaser of Vibe, her upcoming film directed by Kunal Khemu. Zinta recently recalled how Manisha Koirala made her feel she ‘belonged’ in Bollywood during the Dil Se years.
articles.nri_angle: Zinta, an NRI living in the US, is returning to Hindi cinema with a film backed by Amazon MGM Studios — a comeback story with direct resonance for diaspora audiences who grew up on her films.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: 'Why Are Kashmiri Actors Always Terrorists?': Bollywood's Typecasting Debate
articles.excerpt: Filmmakers and critics say Hindi cinema keeps casting Kashmiri performers in one role — the militant — and rarely lets them play anything else.
articles.image_caption: A poster for The Kashmir Files featuring Anupam Kher as Pushkar Nath Pandit. The film sits at the centre of the debate over how Kashmiri characters — and Kashmiri actors — are portrayed in Bollywood.
articles.nri_angle: For diaspora audiences who often encounter Kashmir only through Hindi films, Bollywood's militant-only portrayal shapes the primary image of the Valley they will ever see.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The 'Carbon Copy' Film That Pakistan Banned: The Story of Bedari and Jagriti
articles.excerpt: Pakistan's 1957 patriotic hit Bedari was a scene-for-scene copy of India's Jagriti — and once audiences realised, the ban triggered an uproar.
articles.image_caption: India's 1954 patriotic classic Jagriti, a beloved film about a young reformer's journey. Pakistan's 1957 Urdu film Bedari was later exposed as a scene-for-scene copy of it, and banned after audiences found out.
articles.nri_angle: The Bedari-Jagriti saga is a beloved anecdote of the subcontinent's shared film heritage, resonating with diaspora audiences nostalgic for the pre-Partition cultural world.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Karnataka High Court Grants Actor Duniya Vijay Divorce, Orders Rs 2 Crore Alimony
articles.excerpt: A division bench dissolved the actor's 27-year marriage on grounds of cruelty, overturning a Bengaluru family court ruling, and ordered a Rs 2 crore one-time settlement within two months.
articles.image_caption: Kannada actor Duniya Vijay. The Karnataka High Court has granted him divorce, ordering Rs 2 crore in alimony.
articles.nri_angle: Kannada and Indian diaspora audiences follow Sandalwood legal dramas closely, and the Rs 2 crore figure will be read as a benchmark in celebrity divorce settlements.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Deepika Padukone and Ranveer Singh Share Rare Family Photos on Daughter Dua's Birthday
articles.excerpt: The couple released a series of intimate black-and-white photographs with their daughter on her second birthday, giving fans a rare glimpse of their growing family as they prepare for their second child.
articles.image_caption: Bollywood actress Deepika Padukone. She and husband Ranveer Singh shared rare family photos on their daughter Dua's first birthday.
articles.nri_angle: Bollywood's most celebrated couple gives fans worldwide a rare glimpse into their growing family as they prepare for their second child.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indian Cult Classic 'English, August' Restored in 4K for Venice Film Festival Premiere
articles.excerpt: Film Heritage Foundation rebuilt Dev Benegal's 1994 debut from surviving 35mm prints after the original negatives were destroyed, marking India's third consecutive Venice Classics selection.
articles.image_caption: Dev Benegal's 1994 debut film English, August has been restored in 4K by the Film Heritage Foundation for its Venice Film Festival premiere.
articles.nri_angle: The film's themes of cultural displacement and identity caught between two worlds resonate deeply with Indian diaspora audiences navigating dual identities.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: How Bollywood's Casting Directors Went From Sidelines to Creative Powerhouses
articles.excerpt: Forbes India's Showstoppers 2026 edition spotlights the rise of casting directors as creative collaborators who are reshaping Indian cinema by championing fresh talent over star power.
articles.image_caption: Forbes India's Showstoppers 2026 edition recognises casting directors as key creative collaborators who have transformed how Bollywood discovers and uses talent.
articles.nri_angle: The democratisation of casting in Bollywood has opened doors for actors from small towns across India and even internationally, giving diaspora audiences a wider range of authentic Indian stories on screen.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Anuparna Roy Returns to Venice With Mumbai Migration Drama 'Lovers in the Blue Night'
articles.excerpt: The West Bengal filmmaker, who won Best Director at Venice's Orizzonti section last year, becomes one of the few Indian directors with two consecutive films in competition at the festival.
articles.image_caption: Filmmaker Anuparna Roy, whose second feature Lovers in the Blue Night will premiere at the 83rd Venice International Film Festival on September 11.
articles.nri_angle: Indian independent cinema gains rare global platform as a filmmaker from rural West Bengal earns back-to-back Venice selections, raising the profile of Indian stories on the world stage.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: 'Dil Chahta Hai' at 25: The Film Nobody Wanted to Make That Changed Hindi Cinema
articles.excerpt: Farhan Akhtar's directorial debut turned 25 in August 2026 with a cast reunion and the launch of Excel Origins, a new initiative to find the next generation of filmmakers.
articles.image_caption: Filmmaker Farhan Akhtar, who directed and co-wrote the 2001 coming-of-age classic Dil Chahta Hai, now marking its 25th anniversary.
articles.nri_angle: Dil Chahta Hai was among the first Hindi films that resonated universally with NRI audiences without needing cultural context; its portrayal of friendship across distance spoke to a generation navigating identity abroad.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Irumudi Crosses ₹215 Crore Worldwide as Ravi Teja Scores Biggest Blockbuster of His Career
articles.excerpt: The Telugu action drama has grossed ₹187 crore in India alone after 17 days, with the ₹200 crore domestic milestone now within reach — all without hiked ticket prices.
articles.image_caption: A poster for Irumudi, the Telugu action drama starring Ravi Teja. The film has crossed ₹215 crore worldwide, making it the biggest blockbuster of his career.
articles.nri_angle: Irumudi's career-best overseas gross of ₹20.50 crore underscores Ravi Teja's growing following among Telugu diaspora audiences worldwide.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: From Rs 20 a Day to Box-Office Headliner: Tamil Star Soori's Improbable Rise
articles.excerpt: The former daily-wage worker turned comedy sidekick has delivered four consecutive Rs 50 crore-plus hits since Vetrimaaran's Viduthalai launched his reinvention.
articles.image_caption: Tamil actor Soori at a press event. Once earning Rs 20 a day, Soori has risen to become one of Tamil cinema's leading box-office draws.
articles.nri_angle: Soori's reinvention from comedy sidekick to leading man mirrors Tamil cinema's growing reach among global diaspora audiences following regional hits.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Mamitha Baiju's Health Scare Puts Spotlight on Her Unprecedented Rs 200 Crore Streak
articles.excerpt: The 25-year-old Malayalam actress was hospitalized after delivering three consecutive Rs 200 crore-plus blockbusters in under two months, drawing nationwide attention for the first time.
articles.image_caption: Malayalam actress Mamitha Baiju. Her consecutive box-office hits have collectively grossed over Rs 200 crore.
articles.nri_angle: Mamitha's viral moment highlights the growing crossover of South Indian cinema stars into the broader diaspora consciousness, especially as regional films dominate box-office charts globally.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Drishyam: The Conclusion Trailer Drops September 9 Ahead of Gandhi Jayanti Release
articles.excerpt: Ajay Devgn returns as Vijay Salgaonkar in the final chapter of Hindi cinema's most successful thriller franchise, with Jaideep Ahlawat and Prakash Raj joining the ensemble for an October 2 theatrical release.
articles.nri_angle: The Drishyam franchise is hugely popular among Indian diaspora audiences in the US, who have followed both the Malayalam and Hindi versions of Vijay Salgaonkar's story.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Asur Season 3 Begins Shooting With Arshad Warsi and Barun Sobti, Eyes Mid-2027 Premiere
articles.excerpt: India's acclaimed mythological thriller returns with its original leads plus new additions Ahsaas Channa and Shweta Basu Prasad, as creator Gaurav Shukla steps behind the camera for the first time.
articles.image_caption: Actor Arshad Warsi, who leads the cast of Asur. The thriller series has begun shooting its third season, with co-star Barun Sobti returning alongside the ensemble cast.
articles.nri_angle: Asur has been a breakout Indian streaming hit for NRI audiences, with JioHotstar's international platform ensuring global access for Season 3
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Onslaught — Critics Say Adam Wingard's Latest is a Mixed Bag of Action and Horror
articles.excerpt: The film receives mixed reviews, with some praising its nostalgic elements while others criticize its execution.
articles.image_caption: 'Onslaught' directed by Adam Wingard, now in theaters.
articles.nri_angle: As an English-language film, it is easily accessible for diaspora audiences. However, its reliance on genre tropes may not resonate with everyone.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Mirzapur: The Movie — Critics Say Pankaj Tripathi and Ali Fazal Deliver a Thrilling Return to the Underworld
articles.excerpt: Critics are largely positive about the film, praising its engaging narrative and performances despite some concerns over its length.
articles.image_caption: Pankaj Tripathi stars in Mirzapur: The Movie, which released in theaters worldwide.
articles.nri_angle: The film is available with subtitles, making it accessible for non-Hindi speakers in the diaspora. Fans of the series will find it a satisfying continuation of the story.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Sony Sets November 6 Global Release for Ramayana With Ranbir Kapoor, Yash, and Sai Pallavi
articles.excerpt: The first Indian film to receive the 'Filmed for IMAX' label will get a worldwide theatrical release from Sony Pictures, timed to coincide with Diwali festivities.
articles.image_caption: Ranbir Kapoor stars as Lord Ram in Ramayana: Part One, set for a worldwide release on November 6, 2026 through Sony Pictures.
articles.nri_angle: Sony's global distribution marks the first time a Hollywood studio has given a mainstream worldwide theatrical release to an Indian film, with diaspora audiences expected to drive significant turnout alongside crossover appeal.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Toxic English Version Hits Indian Screens Today With Tighter 18-Minute Shorter Cut
articles.excerpt: The English version of Yash's pan-India gangster drama arrives in Indian cinemas on September 4 with a leaner runtime, even as the film's box office trajectory remains a talking point after a sharp post-opening decline.
articles.image_caption: Yash stars in Toxic: A Fairy Tale for Grown-Ups, whose English version releases in Indian cinemas on September 4 with an 18-minute shorter cut.
articles.nri_angle: Lionsgate acquired international English distribution rights to target non-diaspora audiences in western theatrical chains, while Phars Film handles the five Indian-language versions overseas.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Mirzapur: The Movie Opens Today With 90,000 Tickets Sold, Eyes Rs 30 Crore Debut
articles.excerpt: India's first OTT-to-theatrical franchise film has sold 90,000 advance tickets in top cinema chains, with industry insiders projecting a Rs 100 crore opening weekend.
articles.image_caption: Pankaj Tripathi, who returns as Kaleen Bhaiya in Mirzapur: The Movie, released on September 4, 2026.
articles.nri_angle: The Mirzapur franchise has a massive following among Indian diaspora audiences who streamed the original series on Amazon Prime Video, making it a cultural touchstone for NRIs worldwide.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
